Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufic.fact: Sheila S. Blair suggests that "the name Kufic was introduced to Western scholarship by Jacob Georg Christian Adler (1756–1834)".

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: In fact, "it is the first style of _____ period writings in which the manifestation of art, delicacy and beauty are explicitly evident", says Salwa Ibraheem Tawfeeq Al-Amin
Kufic.fact: Furthermore, the Kufic script plays an important role in the development of Islamic calligraphy. In fact, "it is the first style of Islamic period writings in which the manifestation of art, delicacy and beauty are explicitly evident", says Salwa Ibraheem Tawfeeq Al-Amin.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: Around the 8th century, it was the most important of several variants of _____ scripts with its austere and fairly low vertical profile and a horizontal emphasis
Kufic.fact: Around the 8th century, it was the most important of several variants of Arabic scripts with its austere and fairly low vertical profile and a horizontal emphasis.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: Until about the 11th century it was the main script used to copy the _____
Kufic.fact: Until about the 11th century it was the main script used to copy the Quran. Professional copyists employed a particular form of Kufic for reproducing the earliest surviving copies of the Quran, which were written on parchment and date from the 8th to 10th centuries.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: It is distinguished from _____ script in its use of decorative elements whereas the latter was designed to avoid decorative motifs
Kufic.fact: It is distinguished from Thuluth script in its use of decorative elements whereas the latter was designed to avoid decorative motifs. In place of the decorations in Kufic scripts, Thuluth used vowels.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: However, it is still used in _____ countries
Kufic.fact: However, it is still used in Islamic countries.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: It is commonly attributed to the early _____ or Abbasid court
Kufic.fact: It is commonly attributed to the early Fatimid or Abbasid court.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: The main text of this _____ is written in gold ink, thus the effect on looking at the manuscript is of gold on blue
Kufic.fact: One impressive example of an early Quran manuscript, called the Blue Quran, features gold Kufic script on parchment dyed with indigo. The main text of this Quran is written in gold ink, thus the effect on looking at the manuscript is of gold on blue.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: In fact, "the letter strokes on coins, had become perfectly straight, with curves tending toward geometrical circularity by 86", observes _____
Kufic.fact: In fact, "the letter strokes on coins, had become perfectly straight, with curves tending toward geometrical circularity by 86", observes Alain George.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: Its decorative character led to its use as a decorative element in several public and domestic buildings constructed prior to the _____ period in Turkey
Kufic.fact: Its decorative character led to its use as a decorative element in several public and domestic buildings constructed prior to the Republican period in Turkey.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufic.fact: Also, the current flag of Iraq (2008) also includes a kufic rendition of the takbir.

Kufic.fact: Similarly, the flag of Iran (1980) has the takbir written in white square kufic script a total of 22 times on the fringe of both the green and red bands.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufic.fact: Invented in Iraq, it was prominently used in Iranian architecture with bricks and tiles functioning as pixels.

Kufic.fact: In recent years, this calligraphy form has been receiving more popularity for use in ornaments (such as in decorated clocks, frames, stickers), logos (that usually implies Islamic enterprises in government and private sectors), and even in freestyle Arabic calligraphy competitions. This controlled method of creation preserved basic and accurate features of Arabic letters with few compromises, if any.

Kufic.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufic.question: Linear is preferred to write long scriptures such as _____ verses along the interior perimeter or broken into lines elegantly against mosque walls
Kufic.fact: Linear is preferred to write long scriptures such as Quranic verses along the interior perimeter or broken into lines elegantly against mosque walls.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufra.question: The _____ was Place in Cyrenaica, Libya.
Kufra.fact: Kufra () is a basin and oasis group in the Kufra District of southeastern Cyrenaica in Libya. At the end of the 19th century, Kufra became the centre and holy place of the Senussi order.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufra.question: It also played a minor role in the _____ of World War II
Kufra.fact: It also played a minor role in the Western Desert Campaign of World War II.

Kufra.fact: For the colonial Italians, it was also important as a station on the north-south air route to Italian East Africa.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufra.fact: The term kafir originates from the Arabic root K-F-R, which means "to cover" or "to conceal".

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufra.fact: In Islamic theology, it refers to someone who denies or conceals the truth of Islam, with reference to the Toubou people native to the region. Arab tribes—primarily the Zuwayya and Jawabis—sought to assert control over the region’s most fertile oases, a core area of Toubou settlement.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufra.question: Arab tribes—primarily the _____ and Jawabis—sought to assert control over the region’s most fertile oases, a core area of Toubou settlement
Kufra.fact: Arab tribes—primarily the Zuwayya and Jawabis—sought to assert control over the region’s most fertile oases, a core area of Toubou settlement.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufra.fact: Contemporary accounts, such as those by the German explorer Friedrich Hornemann (1772–1801), who crossed the Libyan Desert in 1798, document the early invasions into Toubou-controlled territory.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufra.fact: The first Arab invasions, carried out by the Jawazi tribes from northern Cyrenaica in the late 18th and early 19th centuries, were met with local resistance and ultimately repelled.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufra.question: A pivotal moment occurred in _____, during the rule of Yusuf Karamanli, Pasha of Tripoli
Kufra.fact: A pivotal moment occurred in 1808, during the rule of Yusuf Karamanli, Pasha of Tripoli.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufra.question: After facing strong local resistance, Arab tribes sought military aid from the _____ authorities
Kufra.fact: After facing strong local resistance, Arab tribes sought military aid from the Ottoman authorities. However, Kufra never fully came under the dominion of either the Arabs or the Ottomans.

Kufra.question: These military campaigns reportedly resulted in significant casualties among the native Toubou (Goran) and _____ populations and many were forced migrate from the region
Kufra.fact: These military campaigns reportedly resulted in significant casualties among the native Toubou (Goran) and Zaghawa populations and many were forced migrate from the region.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufra.fact: In response, they were supplied with firearms and troops, leading to the occupation of the Kufra region—one of the Toubou's strongholds—by the Zuwayya and their allies. These military campaigns reportedly resulted in significant casualties among the native Toubou (Goran) and Zaghawa populations and many were forced migrate from the region.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufra.fact: Historically, southern Cyrenaica was known in prehistoric times for its fertility and verdant landscape.

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kufra.question: Concerning the _____, Herodotus' descriptions are contradictory, raising critical questions about the reliability of his ethnographic accounts
Kufra.fact: Concerning the Garamantes, Herodotus' descriptions are contradictory, raising critical questions about the reliability of his ethnographic accounts. Kufra.fact: These are the same people, from the same place who are the Nasamones, who clearly provided geographic descriptions and oral accounts to the Greek historian Herodotus. Kufra.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kufra.fact: The Toubou are also called Goran, a name that is still in use today particularly in Sudan.

Kufra.fact: In fact, these names are used interchangeably in the Tubu world, just like the ancient names Tehenu and Temehu, which the ancient Egyptians used to refer to the same people.

Kufra.fact: It is attributed to them through their ancestors, the Garamantes—Garama–nte—Herodotus derived their name from their city of Garama, (also called Germa but locally pronounced as Jarma).
